successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: the county of Toulouse under Alphonse of Poitiers, 'Acquired by France: 1271'

ledger.x: 990: the County of Toulouse, established by Charlemagne in 778 according to the page's infobox, is drawn from Cliopatria's first shape.
Page silent on 1066: Cliopatria adds its County of Rouergue shape (27.9k km2, reaching the Rhône) to Toulouse in 1066.
1209: the Albigensian Crusade takes Béziers (22 July) and Carcassonne (15 August); in autumn 'Simon de Montfort is granted control of the area encompassing Carcassonne, Albi, and Béziers'.

1215: at the Fourth Lateran Council Simon de Montfort is proclaimed Count of Toulouse: 'Lands of Raymond VI conquered by the crusade go to Simon, and unconquered lands are placed under Church protection until Raymond VII comes of age.'
1224: Carcassonne and the Trencavel lands return.
1226: Louis VIII's crusade takes the Languedoc coast.
1229: the Treaty of Paris, signed at Meaux on 12 April 1229, ends the war.

1229: Raymond VII 'ceded more than half his land to the French crown' and gave up 'the eastern provinces of his lands'; the Raymond VII page adds that he 'ceded the former Trencavel viscounty to Louis IX'.
1242: after the Saintonge War Raymond VII is 'forced to surrender Saverdun and Bram' to Louis IX.

1249: Raymond VII dies at Toulouse on 27 September without a male heir; 'Alphonse became count of Toulouse' with Joan, and the county passes from the house of Saint-Gilles to the Capetian count of Poitiers: same state and colour.
1271: Alphonse of Poitiers dies at Savona on 21 August 1271 'without heirs' and the county passes to the French crown.

wars.name: Albigensian Crusade
wars.outcome: The crusade took the Trencavel lands (1209), made Simon de Montfort count of Toulouse (1215), lost them again to Raymond VI and VII (1217-1224), and ended with Louis VIII's campaign of 1226 and the Treaty of Paris of 12 April 1229.

wars.name: Siege of Toulouse (1159)
wars.outcome: 'In 1159, Eleanor and Henry unsuccessfully tried to enforce her claim to Toulouse through her grandmother'; no ground changed hands.

wars.name: Saintonge War
wars.outcome: Raymond VII allied with Hugh of La Marche and Henry III of England against Louis IX in 1242 and was 'forced to surrender Saverdun and Bram'.

certainty.note: Feudal frontiers drawn from regions; the Treaty of Paris of 1229 cedes the 'eastern provinces' without a boundary on any page opened.
